messages:
alana: Short follow-up to the quant profiles RFC. I want to propose a concrete runtime pattern: explicit 'precision safepoints' + a transient dispatch context that lasts until the next safepoint.
mike: Curious where you put safepoints. whole-layer only? inside attention?
jess: Layer boundaries only, otherwise KV cache + attention state would require conversions mid-kv. My suggestion: place safepoint after layernorm and before heavy matmul ops.
alana: Yes. two canonical safepoints: (1) post-layernorm -> pre-attn, (2) post-attn -> pre-ffn. That keeps caches intact and limits state conversions.
zach: Our kernel registry is op x dtype x hw. If we let the runtime pick kernels at each op we blow up combinatorics.
alana: To avoid that we propose mapping (op, profile-hint) -> ordered kernel candidates. At each safepoint the runtime evaluates a tiny profile-hint (preferred bitwidths + fallback order + affinity tag) and sets a dispatch context that subsequent ops consult.
mike: So per-op metadata is tiny, we set the full policy at a few points instead of every op. Good for metadata bloat.
jess: Operationally we need overrides: canary per-customer, per-endpoint opt-in. How does that get into the dispatch context?
alana: Endpoint config can include precision_policy which merges into the dispatch context when the first safepoint for that request is hit. We can also support per-request overrides via headers, but only as an override token applied at safepoint.
nisha: Telemetry: at every safepoint emit which dispatch policy was selected, which kernel ended up being used for each op group, and any fallback events. Also sample a few outputs when a fallback chain occurs for QA.
zach: Adding safepoints sounds like a scheduling barrier. Any perf numbers?
alana: Measured locally: safepoint check ~40ns, selecting policy & setting context ~300-600ns per boundary. For a 48-layer model that is ~30us worst case, trivial compared to per-layer kernel time.
mike: How do we handle sharded models where different shards compute different layer ranges on different devices? The dispatch context must be consistent across shards.
alan a: Two patterns: (A) centralized coordinator pushes context to shards before they run; (B) deterministic policy derivation so each shard computes the same context independently from stable inputs (model id, endpoint policy, request seed). I prefer B for lower latency.
jess: Deterministic approach requires a tiny canonical input for policy generation. model version + endpoint policy + per-request seed should be stable.
zach: If a chosen kernel fails at runtime (OOM, assert), we need an atomic fallback to the next candidate and emit telemetry + optionally snapshot debug data.
ops-bot: alert-rule: if runtime-fallback-rate > 0.5% for 5m in prod, create incident; if >2% escalate to paging.
nisha: QA: add a small harness that replays dispatch traces (labelled e.g., safepoint_trace_id) across quant kernels and compares logprobs/embeddings against a golden within thresholds. Also test fallback chains explicitly.
mike: SDK/API: expose simple friendly presets ("throughput-first", "quality-first") that map to internal precision_policy. Keep raw precision controls gated behind advanced flags.
jess: Good. also ensure quant-table serialization is versioned and checksummed so runtimes verify compatibility before applying a policy.
alana: Implementation plan (MVP):
  1) compiler IR: add safepoint markers + runtime hook (1.5w)
  2) runtime: transient dispatch context + policy merge (2w)
  3) kernel registry: support ordered candidate lists per (op, hint) (1.5w)
  4) telemetry + QA harness + canary plan (1.5w)
Estimate ~7 weeks end-to-end for safe MVP, less if we feature-flag a fast path.
zach: Quick experiment idea: feature-flag a global enforced policy (--force-dispatch=policyX) to run full-model tests without adding safepoint plumbing. Quick sanity checks for kernels & fallbacks.
alana: Good idea. We'll use that to validate candidate kernels at scale before landing safepoints.
nisha: Add telemetry tag for quant-table-version and dispatch-generator-seed for easier postmortems.
mike: Who picks this up?
alana: I'll own the IR + runtime hook. zach + jess take dispatch table & kernel registry. nisha owns telemetry + QA harness. mike will wire SDK presets.
jess: I'll post a sketch of the dispatch table JSON layout tonight in the PR.
zach: I'll prototype deterministic policy generator for sharded runs this week.
alana: Thanks all. let's sync after the first PRs. :thumbsup:
